subject: [PATCH v9 0/6] mm, iomap, NFSD: stop uncached writes reading back shared pages

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Reviewer suggested that the patch should be taken through the MM tree for review, as it depends on changes to the MM API and NFSD is the first consumer of this work.
reviews.raw_body:
My recommendation was take all of this through the MM tree, since
the NFSD patch looks like the first consumer of the work, and it
depends on how the MM API is changed during review.


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)

2026-10-27.patch_summary: This patch series addresses an issue where uncached writes to shared pages can read back the original contents, rather than the updated data. The problem arises from the interaction between iomap and NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code paths. To fix this, the patches modify the mm and iomap code to ensure that uncached writes are properly handled.

reviews.author: Mike Snitzer
reviews.summary: Reviewer Mike Snitzer noted that the NFSD patch (6/6) requires four prerequisite changes to be staged in the cel/nfsd-testing branch before it can be applied, suggesting a post-merge NFSD tree for kernel version 7.5.
reviews.raw_body:
Chuck, I agree, the mm changes would certainly do well to go through
the mm tree.  But the 6/6 NFSD patch that makes use of the preceding
mm dontcache interface changes requires 4 of the 6 prerequisite
changes to NFSD DIRECT that have have staged in cel/nfsd-testing.

So I think we might need a post-merge NFSD tree for 7.5 that applies
the 6/6 NFSD change ontop of the changes that would land through mm.

Willy, I would like to work with you (and others in mm if they are
interested), Jeff and Chuck between now and April 2027 to see these
changes accepted for the 7.5 merge window. And if that were to happen
I cannot wait to celebrate with all of you at LSF/MM in Portugal!

Thanks,
Mike
